hero.title: Renseikan Kyudojo
hero.lede: Traditional Japanese archery, taught the way it has been for centuries. New students are always welcome. The first lesson is free with no appointments needed, just walk in during a regularly scheduled class time.

glance.title: The dojo at a glance
federation: The founding dojo of the [Northern California Kyudo Federation]({nckf}) (NCKF), which is a founding member of the [American Kyudo Renmei]({akr}).

expect.title: Beginning Your Kyudo Journey
expect.subtitle: What to expect
expect.lede: No uniform or equipment is required and no prior experience is necessary.

steps.title: Etiquette first
steps.text: Practice begins with a bow to the shōmen, the front of the hall: the tokonoma (picture alcove) and the national flag. You learn how to enter the hall and where to stand before you draw a bow.

steps.title: Form before arrows
steps.text: You learn the eight stages of shooting (shahō hassetsu) with a rubber practice bow called a gomuyumi. Then you draw a real bow without an arrow (subiki), first bare-handed and then wearing the glove. Wear loose clothing you can move freely in.

steps.title: Makiwara, then the mato
steps.text: Your first arrows go to the makiwara, a straw target shot at close range. Once your form is steady you move on to the mato at 28 metres.

about.seoDescription: What kyudo is, the dojo's name 練誠館 (Hall of Sincere Training), its history since the mid-1970s, and its place in the Northern California Kyudo Federation and the American Kyudo Renmei.
about.title: 練誠館, the Renseikan
about.lede: Kyudo (弓道, "the way of the bow") is Japanese archery practised as a discipline: one arrow at a time, the same eight movements, the same breathing. {name} teaches it every Sunday at the Japanese Art & Cultural Center (JACC) in San Jose, California.

sections.title: The name
body: 練 *ren* is to train, to refine; 誠 *sei* is sincerity; 館 *kan* is the hall. Together, the Hall of Sincere Training.

sections.title: History
body: The Renseikan began as the San Jose Kyudo Club, formed in the mid-1970s. The club was the original founding dojo of the [Northern California Kyudo Federation]({nckf}) (NCKF), which Japan accepted as a foreign *renmei* in 1981.
Sensei Steve Scott renamed the San Jose Kyudo Club the Renseikan in 2003, a few years after the Kurumi-an dojo in San Jose closed in 1999.

sections.title: What a class looks like
body: The dojo usually sets up three makiwara (straw practice targets shot at close range) and students take turns at them and at the mato 28 metres away. Beginners learn the eight stages of the shot (the *shahō hassetsu*) with a rubber practice bow called a gomuyumi, then draw one of the dojo's bows without an arrow (*subiki*), first bare-handed and then with the glove. The first arrows go to the makiwara, and the mato comes once the form is steady. Nothing is rushed and a class has room for everyone to shoot.
Members who have been invited also practise on Saturdays at Redwood Kyudojo.

sections.title: Affiliation
body: Renseikan, formerly the San Jose Kyudo Club, is the founding dojo of the [Northern California Kyudo Federation]({nckf}) (NCKF), which is a founding member of the [American Kyudo Renmei]({akr}).

join.title: From your first lesson on

steps.title: Your first lesson
body: Walk in during any class, {days} {hours}, at the Japanese Art & Cultural Center. It is free, there is nothing to book and nothing to bring beyond loose clothing you can kneel in and socks. You will learn how to enter the hall and the eight stages of the shot with a rubber practice bow. Over the following lessons you draw a real bow without an arrow, then with the glove, and then shoot your first arrows at the makiwara.

steps.title: After that
body: Regular classes are booked through the Japanese Art & Cultural Center (JACC) on WellnessLiving. Ask the instructor about membership and class fees at your first visit, or email {email}.

steps.title: Equipment
body: The dojo provides the bow, glove and arrows during practice. There is no hurry to buy your own: the glove has to fit your hand, and the bow and arrows have to fit your body, so the instructor will help you choose them when you are ready.

fees.title: Fees

entries.question: Do I need any experience?
answer: No. Most people who walk in have never held a bow. The first lessons are about posture, breathing and the sequence of the shot: a rubber practice bow first, then a real bow drawn without an arrow, then the glove and the first arrows.

entries.question: How much does the first lesson cost?
answer: Nothing. The first lesson is free and needs no booking: come to any class, {days} {hours}.

entries.question: What should I wear?
answer: Loose clothing you can kneel and raise your arms in, and socks. No uniform is needed to start.

entries.question: Do I need my own bow?
answer: No. The dojo provides the bow, glove and arrows during practice. Your own come later, chosen with the instructor to fit you.

entries.question: Do I have to book?
answer: New students do not. Members reserve their place through the Japanese Art & Cultural Center on WellnessLiving.

entries.question: When do I shoot at the target?
answer: First at the makiwara, a straw target shot at close range, once you can draw a real bow with the glove and the form is in place. The mato at 28 metres comes once the form is steady. Nothing is rushed.

ja.seoDescription: カリフォルニア州サンノゼの弓道場。毎週{days} {hours}、日本芸術文化センター（JACC）にて稽古。初心者歓迎、初回無料、予約不要。
ja.title: 練誠館弓道場
ja.lede: カリフォルニア州サンノゼにある弓道場です。毎週{days}、{hours}に日本芸術文化センター（JACC）で稽古をしています。初心者の方も歓迎します。初回の稽古は無料で、予約は不要です。道着や道具は要りません。経験も問いません。
ja.affiliation: 北カリフォルニア弓道連盟（NCKF）創設道場。NCKFは米国弓道連盟（AKR）の創設メンバーです。

sections.title: はじめての方へ
body: 稽古の時間中にそのままお越しください。はじめは射場への入り方と礼法、ゴム弓での射法八節から始め、素引き、ゆがけをつけての素引きを経て、巻藁で初めて矢を射ます。弓・ゆがけ・矢は稽古中に道場のものを使います。動きやすい服装と靴下でお越しください。

sections.title: 道場について
body: 練誠館は1970年代半ばにサンノゼ弓道クラブとして始まり、1981年に日本から外国連盟として認められた北カリフォルニア弓道連盟の創設道場です。2003年にスコット先生が練誠館と改名しました。
